utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are very sorry about the delay of the witness this morning. The registrar has been instructed to look into this matter and give us an explanation. This kind of thing should never happen to us again because we don't have much time to lose. Mr. Scott, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, we will call the next witness out of turn. Mr. Bos will be handling that witness, and he will give the particulars in terms of protective measures and the way forward, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. The next witness is a witness who has also requested some protective measures. He requested a pseudonym, and he requested facial distortion. I think it has already been set up. So if there's no objection from the Defence, I hope these protective measures can be granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It seems to me that there are no objections from Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So the protective measures have been granted by this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pseudonym for this witness is Witness T. Exhibit Number PW21.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we are waiting for the witness, the witness will testify about paragraphs 14 to 17 in the indictment, which go to the superior authority of the accused, as well as paragraph 29 of the indictment relating to Count 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper shown by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, can you move the screen a bit, because I'm not able to see you, Witness. Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can you move a little bit closer to the microphone, please. Witness, the Trial Chamber has granted some protective measures for you. They have granted the measures of pseudonym and facial distortion. Now, in order for the protective measure of a pseudonym to be -- for that protective measure, you're going to be shown a paper, which the usher has right in front of you, and the paper shows your name and the letter of the pseudonym you're going to get. You see it says "Witness T," and then is that your name which is underneath there? Could you just confirm without mentioning your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So in the course of my examination, I'll be referring to you as "Witness T." Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness T, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What is your ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, were you ever a member of the KB Krusko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you remember when you became a member of that unit, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: In the beginning of '93 until '96.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And where was this unit stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: In the beginning, at the Heliodrom, and then in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And who commanded that unit in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnic origin of Mr. Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And do you know where he is from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did this man, Juka Prazina, did he have anything to do with the fact that you joined this unit, this unit KB Krusko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, let me try to rephrase it. The man you've been referring to as "Juka Prazina," was he one of the reasons why you joined this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain how it came about that you joined this unit, KB Krusko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It happened when we came out of Sarajevo to deblock the city. We came out as special units of the BH army, and then a conflict broke out on Mount Igman between Zuka and Juka, as we say - I don't know why - so that we ended up in Mostar as members of the Convicts' Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: This man, Juka, did you also serve under this man in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And so you were saying that there was a conflict which broke out on Mount Igman between Juka and another man named "Zuka." And as a result of that conflict, did Juka leave Mount Igman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And you followed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you said that you joined the KB Krusko which was stationed at the Heliodrom. I'm going to show you a photograph which is marked as Exhibit 20.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask if this can be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can you see this photograph, Witness? Witness T, do you recognise this photograph, what's depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: This is the Heliodrom barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And do you recognise the building on this photograph in which you were stationed at the Heliodrom barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: In the first building to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can he be given a pointer so he can point on the photograph which building he's referring to? Yes. You can put the photograph under the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you're depicting the building on the left-hand side, right in front of the building with the red roof. Is that the building you were staying in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said you were a member of a unit called the "KB Krusko." What does "KB" stand for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: "Convicts' Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of the Convicts' Battalion was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Tell us his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Tuta, Naletilic. Mladen, Tuta, Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: This Convicts' Battalion, did it have any other units except for the unit you joined, except for the unit Krusko, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can you try to tell us which other units you are aware of, and maybe also who commanded those units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Kaznjenicka Bojna-Krusko; commander, Juka Prazina. Stela, then, Vinko Martinovic, Stela. I think it was called "Mrmak." And then there was Baja Martinovic -- not Martinovic -- Baja. And there were some others whose names I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's go to the first one you said. You say a unit called the KB Mrmak, which was commanded by a man named "Stela." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the witness speak out, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever meet this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where did you meet Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: In passing, around the town, coffee shops and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know where the headquarters was of this unit called KB Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It was at Liska, I think it is called, a park Liska, and I know there was a pharmacy nearby and a school.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Which town was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you also referred to a man named "Baja." Do you know which unit he commanded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: ATG. Don't know what his name was. Can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Is "Baja" a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you don't know any other names for this person except "Baja"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Baja Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And do you recall any other units or commanders of units from the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: There were some other units. I know a nickname here and there, but I don't know the names. There was something which was called Tango or Tanger or something that sounded like that. And -- I don't know. In Mostar, I don't really know any other names.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: This "Tanger," this referred also to a unit in Mostar or to a commander in a unit in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The name of the commander of the unit in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness T, when you said that you joined the KB Krusko in early 1993, how many members did this KB Krusko have at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: About 90. There were men and women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You said that the unit was -- included men, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what about the ethnic composition of this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Members came from all ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When you started to join this unit, were you given a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did the uniform also have a patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: HVO in the early days, in the beginning. After that, ATG, Convicts' Battalion, Krusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Were you issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: We had our own weapons that we had brought with us. And later on, individuals were issued with other weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, what were your duties in the KB Krusko in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At first, we provided the front lines for a while, and then I became a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So if we're talking about the beginning of '93, this was the confrontation line against the Serbs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You said that after that, you became a driver. What did you transport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Everything: people to front lines, food, and wherever one had to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You said that you transported food. Where would you get that food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: We had food at Heliodrom, but we additionally also provided some food because there was a Caritas depot at Siroki and there was a warehouse at Siroki within the Convicts' Battalion from where we got food and juices Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and other necessities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You're saying you got food from the Caritas warehouses in Siroki. Is that Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And for whom was this food, if you got food from there? To whom would you deliver that food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At first, to those 90 soldiers, men, women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: And later, I went to Croatia, taking it to the wounded and those who were not wounded who were in Promajna, that is, in Juka Prazina's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But you would always -- not wounded. Would it still be delivering to soldiers or also to civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: "Yes" meaning also to civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, in order to get that food from the Caritas warehouses, did you need a paper or could you just go there and take the food out of the warehouses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I had to have a document which was signed by Juka Prazina. He would make a list on numerical strength, and that is how we were issued those documents. And later on, other commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you said that you also got food from a warehouse which was stationed at the headquarters, at the KB headquarters. Where was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: We call that "Tobacco Factory," because that is where it was at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that the commander of the KB was Mladen Naletilic. Did you ever see this man when you would collect food from the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could you describe how he looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Please give us a description.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Medium height, about 60 to 70 kilograms, hair grey or, rather, greying, a beard, and he always wore glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sorry, we couldn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And how did people refer to Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: "Tuta," and my commander of late began to call him "Stari."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When you refer to your commander, whom do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Bozo Sajin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you see Tuta also on other spots than just the headquarters? Did you ever see him somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I used to see him around Siroki, then once at the Heliodrom - I don't remember when - and then at a funeral of one of the fallen combatants. I used to see him -- I saw him on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's first go to this funeral of a combatant. Do you remember whose funeral that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember. I don't know who it was that was killed. I know it was at Masline.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You also testified that you once saw Tuta at the Heliodrom. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: With whom did you see him there, and what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He passed by the building that we were quartered and went to the other end of the barracks, where the main -- what do you call it? Where the command was. I don't know whether he went to the command, but he walked towards the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you see him with a particular person on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: There was Juka Prazina and there were some others whom I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What was the relationship between Tuta and Juka Prazina, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I believe they were good.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Were they friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever heard of a man named "Andabak"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who is he; what was his function?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He was Tuta's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you ever see Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where would you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I saw him at Siroki Brijeg and in Juka Prazina's flat in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you recall that at one moment in Mostar there was an attack on the Vranica building? Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I know the whole story, but I wasn't in Mostar at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the KB Krusko was involved in this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And Mr. Juka Prazina, was he also involved in this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You stated that you yourself were not involved because you were not in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You've stated earlier on that at one point in time, the KB Krusko was relocated from the Heliodrom to Mostar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where did you move in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, we moved next to the stadium, two or three buildings nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: The whole unit moved in one particular place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, those left of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: How many there were left of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: About 30, 35 men, but it changed day in and day out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where had all the others gone, because you testified that you started with about 90 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Some went to Grude. Others were wounded. Two, I believe, were killed. Yes, that's right, two got killed. They went wherever. Those who wanted to go and could fend for themselves, they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Were you just free to go when you were a member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, if Juka agreed to help us, or some other of the more important people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So it depended on the commander of the unit whether you could actually leave the unit if you wanted to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: If he was willing to help us to go somewhere abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You left the Heliodrom. Do you know why you had to leave the Heliodrom, why you moved to another place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. There were all sorts of stories around. But the majority of us were Muslims, and so there were some rumours to that effect, so that I don't know the real result.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: While you were at the Heliodrom, did you ever see that other barracks were used or did you notice that prisoners would also be kept in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The Heliodrom was used for that purpose. I don't know about others.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who were taken prisoner in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Civilians mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what ethnicity had these civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Muslims mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You testified that you moved out of the Heliodrom and moved into Mostar. Juka Prazina, did he also move out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, but a day or two later, he went somewhere, and we did not see him again. After a day or two, a couple of days, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You never saw him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you recall around which period of time approximately you actually moved out of the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date. It could be early '94 or maybe end of '93. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: At the time that you left the Heliodrom, and you testified that Juka had left -- first of all, how did you feel about the fact that Juka had left the unit? How did you feel about it, because you actually joined the unit because you followed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The majority of us felt very down, indeed, because we felt betrayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: At that time, did your unit still fight the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At the time, when we were in Mostar, we did not fight against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you fight against anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, we did, against the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You are a Muslim yourself, and you had to fight the Muslims. Why did you do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That was my livelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: How did you feel about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you try to escape because of this fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I did on a couple of occasions, but since my -- members of my family were in Croatia, I had nowhere to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You said that the members of your family were in Croatia. How did they come there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They got there as refugees in '91.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: At the time that you were in Mostar, they were still in -- as refugees in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, during the time that you were a member of the KB Krusko, did you ever -- were you ever issued permits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, a number of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What was the purpose of these permits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Free exit from Herceg-Bosna to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And from whom would you get these permits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: My commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness T, that you have saved some of these permits and that you handed these permits to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 242. And for the information of the Judges, I've made a set of copies, and also a set of copies for the Defence. These documents are also in the 17 binders, but just for the sake of efficiency, I have made some copies for use here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would like to go over the various permits that you still had in your possession, and I would like you first to look at Exhibit P242. And I don't know if you have that document in front of you. I think it starts with the English translation and then behind it there will be the original version, followed by a French version. Some of these permits will also be translated into French, not all of them, but the majority are.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor, is the exhibit under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All of these exhibits will be tendered under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you have the first permit in front of you. Maybe you can look at the original version, which is a few pages later on. Now, what is the date on this permit, Witness? And please don't refer to your name, because otherwise it would defeat the purpose of your protection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The 2nd of February, 1993, until the 13th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Is it the 2nd or the 6th of February?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The 2nd of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. And what was the purpose of this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: A visit to the relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And where did you travel to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They were at Orebic, so I went to Orebic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where is Orebic, in which state is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Croatia, near Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's look at the persons who signed this permit, and let's first look at the left-hand corner. It's not really a signature there, but Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. there's a man mentioned there by the name of "Miljenko Lasic." Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was the supreme commander of the HVO. He was a commander, like a minister. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: In the right-hand corner, there's a signature. Do you recognise whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I can read it out. I don't know the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, could you please read it out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: "Zelenika."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, if you turn to the next page - it's probably there at the back of the permit - there's a little note there which says -- well, maybe you can read it out and explain what this note is for.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: When I was returning from my visit to my family, I wrote where Juka's house was, near Baske Vode, Promajna, because I didn't know where Promajna was or where Baske Vode were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So it was a personal note to remember where to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next exhibit, which is Exhibit P303. This one does not have a French translation. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe you can look at the original. What's the date on this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: 19 April 1993 until 26th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Visit to my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And by whom is the permit signed? Let's first look in the left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And in the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Jusuf Prazina, Juka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next exhibit, which is P435. And maybe if you can look at the original version. What is the date on this exhibit, on this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: 7th June 1993 until 7th July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And do you recall what the purpose was of this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Visit to the wounded in Split and then Promajna.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And who signed this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Miljenko Lasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And the signature on the right-hand corner, whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Lasic, I suppose, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, let's move on to the next exhibit, Exhibit 501. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What's the date on this exhibit, on this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Issued on July 7th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, I received this in Promajna to be able to enter Herceg-Bosna and to move freely on the territory of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who signed this permit? Let's first look at the left-hand corner again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It was signed by Valentin Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know who Valentin Coric is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And do you recognise the signature on the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on to Exhibit 507. What's the date on this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: 8th July 1993 until 8th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, just to clarify: If it says from 8 July to 8 August '93, what does that mean? Does that mean that the permit was valid until that period or that you actually needed to be back on that particular date, on the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: We had to return by that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And would you always return on that particular date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, not always.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could it be later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, because I was given another permit in Promajna so I could get in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Right. But if you would go over the date of 8 August, you would require another permit; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, what was the purpose of this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Visiting the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And who signed this permit, if you look at the left-hand corner first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And do you recognise the signature on the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Lasic. Miljenko, Mica, Lasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: That's the person you identified before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Finally, could we look at Exhibit 659. What's the date on this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: 24th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Visiting family.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, let's, again, look at the person who signed this permit, person there in the left-hand corner. It's a bit difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Miljenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know who the person is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And whose signature is on the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Bozo Sajin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He replaced Juka Prazina when Juka fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So is it fair to conclude that on the 23rd of October, Juka Prazina no longer commanded the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's move to the second page, because, again, there's some notes on the second page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can you read out what's written there and why it is written there. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, it served as a piece of paper which I had handy with me. It had words of greetings which I had to convey from Munib to the two persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: These persons would live in Croatia, and you would have to convey a message to them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, just for the information of the Trial Chamber, there's also a French translation of this permit. But unfortunately, the name on the French translation reads -- on the left-hand corner reads Miljenko Lasic. I think that that is a mistake because, as we can see on the original, it's not Miljenko Lasic who actually signed this document. It's just for your information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness T. Now, in conclusion, I would like to show you Exhibit P704. This is the exhibit which I think the Trial Chamber is familiar with. It's the long list of names. And I have extracted the page which I needed for this particular witness so you don't have the whole exhibit in front of you. At least, the witness can be shown the complete exhibit with B/C/S or... Now, Witness T, you are shown a document. If you could flip back the page one page and -- I would like him to read the cover page of this document. I don't know if you could... Witness, could you please read out what's on this cover page, and maybe start with the word "Subject." That particular line, could you read it out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Salary list for November 1993. Please find enclosed the salary list for November 1993 for members of the Convicts' Battalion anti-terrorist unit. Commander of the Convicts' Battalion and anti-terrorist unit, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Will you now flip over to the next page. You see a whole list of names. And without mentioning the name, is it correct that number 14, is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And do you recognise the other names in this list of names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who were these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: These were members of the ATJ Krusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, finally, Witness T, how long did the KB Krusko exist? Did there come a time that the name of the unit was changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The name was changed when the 2nd Guards Brigade was formed. And some joined that brigade, and others joined other units and groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you join the 2nd Guards Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Under what army was the 2nd Guards Brigade, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: How long did you remain a member of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: About one year, more or less, perhaps a bit more. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness T, I have one more thing -- I think the witness doesn't need the exhibit any more. Witness T, you have described for us today in court a man by the name of Mladen Naletilic. Could you please look around in this courtroom and see whether you actually recognise this man here today in court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can you describe where he is seated and what he is wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He is sitting in the last row. He's second from the right; he's wearing a grey jacket and a brownish shirt and a red and blue tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness T.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness identified the accused Mladen Naletilic. I now would like to tender the various permits which we just went through, so I would like to tender Exhibits P242, P303, P435, P501, P507, and P659. And that concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have five minutes to the break. So are you going to begin your cross-examination right now, or we may have break at this moment and come back later, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry. Of course, I need a break, because a change of witness occurred. Even before the hearing, I spoke to my learned colleague, and I said that I needed time to prepare for the cross. Well, perhaps I could agree with my colleagues on the matter. I don't want to tire Your Honours with this. I don't know what the plans are for the future with the coming of the other witness. Well, we'll have a break, and then we will continue after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think, you know, in the afternoon, at 2:30, we'll continue with the convicted witness. And if we do not finish that witness at 4.00, we might prolong the sitting a little bit, maybe to 5.00 or 5.30. But anyway, we have to finish that witness today. Now, we'll have our break, about 20 minutes. We'll resume at quarter to 12. Then we'll have a break at 1.00 for the lunchtime. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness T. Let me introduce myself. I'm Kresimir Krsnik, and I'm counsel for Mr. Mladen Naletilic. I will ask you some questions, and I will endeavour to phrase them in a manner to allow you then to answer very briefly and very concisely. I shall be asking you questions about what you personally know, not about what you heard from others. So my first question: You were a member of Juka Prazina's unit in Sarajevo in 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel and witness please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And throughout 1992 until you came out to Igman, you were a member Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of that unit, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will please the witness and counsel pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you hear the interpreters? Please make a pause. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what was that unit's name within the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Special units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how strong was that unit in 1992, prior to Igman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I wouldn't know the exact number. But according to their accreditation numbers, about 7.000, roughly. I wouldn't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Juka Prazina had under his command 7.000 members of that unit, of the special unit; is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I'm saying this is what I read on the accreditations list, that that was the number, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any conflicts between these units and some other units within the army of BH in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the conflict which took place on Igman between Zuka Alispago's unit, was that Zuka Alispago and you; was the -- on the other side, Zuka Alispago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, there was a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Zuka Alispago commanded a special unit called "Black Swans", "Crni Labudovi"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it another special-purpose unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, it was a special-purpose unit outside Sarajevo, and we did not know about them. We, who were in Sarajevo, did not know about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, listen, we always have to see -- do you still live in Sarajevo? Don't give us an address or anything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: With your whole family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Some of them are in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, are you aware that the arrest has been ordered of all the members of Juka Prazina's unit and their detention; that in the end of '92, '93, that he was to be detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I am hearing this from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You do not know that an order was issued to all military units on the ground from Igman to Mostar, that is, the 4th Corps or, rather, its area of responsibility, to arrest its members and bring them, under custody, to the District Court in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You did not know, is it, that Mr. Prazina fled from that and that that was how he arrived in the area of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I know we arrived in the area of Mostar. I do not know if he was fleeing from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Not only Mr. Prazina, all the other members ending with number 129, that is, 129 members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, we did not know why he fled. We didn't know the real reason. We never found out the real reason. I mean, we, individual soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you were in Igman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You do not know that there was fighting between Zuka and Juka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know that Zuka disarmed members of Juka's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you do not know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I did not see that, so I'm telling you I heard about it. I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you did not ask anyone else in the unit about what was going on, you simply followed in Juka's steps. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: In the beginning, we were in disarray. There was nobody to ask. We knew nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when you arrived in the area of Mostar, did HVO offer you protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You were issued an HVO ID on the 16th of February, '93. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do not remember the date, but yes, I was issued with an ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: An order was issued whereby you became an autonomous unit within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: As an autonomous unit, you took part both in actions against Serbs and also in actions against Muslims, for instance, in Bijelo Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Your command, I think, belonged in the North-Eastern Herzegovina sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I can't really understand --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, south-east.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know what is the south-eastern part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, say, the area of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when -- and that is where you received your orders from, orders to go into action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You told my learned friend from the Prosecution that Tuta was your commander. Did you hear that or did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I heard that from my commander, from Juka, and others below him. I -- directly, Tuta never addressed me. Tuta never spoke to me to tell me "I'm your commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In other words, you have no direct knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I have knowledge, again, from my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, we've heard that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That's the only kind of knowledge I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell, please, this Honourable Court, what happened to Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: About the conflict, you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm asking you what happened to him. Is he alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I hear that he is dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you hear this fact from Bozo Sajin? Perhaps can we check it with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it from him and from other individuals. And even from the media, from newspapers and such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. You followed the media. And that is what the media wrote about, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you tell us which newspaper, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I believe it was Dnevni Avaz. His sister -- his sister was to transfer his remains, and I think this article was about that. I believe it was Dnevni Avaz.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Dnevni Avaz, is it the organ of the Party for Democratic Action and which came out in Sarajevo? Is that the paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That paper comes out in Sarajevo. Well -- no, I know that it comes out in Bosnia. Whose organ it is, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, have you heard of the conflict between Juka Prazina and Arif Pasalic, the commander of the 4th Corps, whose area of responsibility was Mostar, Konjic and Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: As far as I know, some of our members, that is, members of the KB Krusko, they were allegedly arrested there, captured there, and he requested an exchange. That is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Juka tried -- they tried to disarm Juka, and then somebody threw a hand grenade, and then there ensued an attack on a building called "Vranica." Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At that time, there were conflicts around. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But do you know that Juka wanted to pay him back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, for a while, he spoke out against everybody, not only against him. Whether that was to be a revenge or something, I don't know what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, I mean perhaps he wanted to pay Arif Pasalic back because the latter wanted to disarm him and detain him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, he could have done this to him, that is, disarm him or something. And revenge, well, that can mean murder, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you about. Did Juka attack Vranica because of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know. I know nothing about that. He knows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you told my learned friend that you were not in Mostar in May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: For a part of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. And tell me, please, if you can, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: With my family, I'd say. I must have been with my family, because I had nowhere else to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now tell me, please, your base at Heliodrom, were there many troops? Apart from your unit, were there many other units there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: There were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, was it also the recruitment centre at Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: A training centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, it later -- it was later on at another time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you went into action against Muslims in Bijelo Polje, was Juka your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind as to tell us, how long did you stay with the HVO, in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Early '93 until, I think, early '96 or end of '95 - I'm not sure - but that was with the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you arrived from Igman with Juka Prazina, 95 per cent or perhaps even more of the members of that unit were Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: There were quite a number of Muslims. I wouldn't know the exact number. But we came from all ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And after that, you continued to fight against the BH army too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: A while ago, my learned friend showed you a number of those permits you were issued. I look at their dates. You practically could get a permit whenever you liked; is that so? And if that bothered you, then why didn't you stay with your family in Croatia and leave that all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: And what would you want me to do in Croatia at that time with nine members of my family if I couldn't go elsewhere, to some other country?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you wanted to go to a third country, to a western democratic country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, I am saying "another country." It could be a third country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean a third country of West European democracies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I mean a third country; that is, not Herzegovina, not Croatia, not former Yugoslavia, that is what I mean. Another country. You can call it "a third country," "a fourth country," or whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no, thank you. I'm only asking you what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I mean all that is not the former Yugoslavia, so that is when I say "another country."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And since you did not get the asylum, right, you decided to stay with the HVO; is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Since I could not get that asylum from those who were my bosses, that is, I could -- as you put it, I could -- yes, I could escape to Croatia. But what then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You would have got the refugee card in Croatia, like your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you had the refugee card in Croatia too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the Croatian State, they would have taken care of you, just as they took care of your family? I don't know, of course, what it amounted Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to, but something they did get so you could stay in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I had this possibility. But whether it was healthy to stay there, to escape one unit with which I had left Sarajevo, to leave that unit, to betray that unit, and that to live within their reach, an hour or two of car ride, what would be the consequences? Would somebody think that I had betrayed him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Your commander betrayed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, in the end. But we remained loyal to him to the very end because we were hoping for something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when did you return to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I think in early '96 or end of '95. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was an investigation started against you in Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: -- because you were a member of Juka Prazina's unit and because you fought against the army of BH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I am not aware of any investigation against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Nobody conducted an interview with you, either in the police or by a judge, no charges were brought against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: There were others who also fought against AbiH army from some other formations and still lived normally. And no charges have been brought against them either, not at least that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: At some point you said that you were hoping for something, so here's my question. Can you tell us, what is it that you hoped for when you stayed in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: When we left Sarajevo, we left intending to deblock Sarajevo. That was our intention and our wish. And by -- and when we joined the HVO, there was no conflict between the Muslims and Croats then. So we hoped that we would altogether set off to open that city, to liberate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you personally aware -- do you know that major Croat forces arrived at Igman joined with Juka Prazina's forces were ready to set out to liberate Sarajevo that you were prevented from doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do not know that, but I have heard of those stories, because I was in Sarajevo at that time. And we then took pride in that fact because we hoped that it would be liberated. But I heard about what you are telling me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did Juka Prazina have a conflict with the Supreme Command because he wanted and supported the plan to deblock Sarajevo, to get away the Croat army and the Supreme Command, and the president of the state would not allow that? Let me repeat my question because not everybody heard it because I'm just too fast. I apologise. I do not wait for the end of the interpretation. That is, are you aware that Juka Prazina, a man who commanded the largest number of men in Sarajevo, endorsed the plan -- when I say the Croat army, always mean the HVO, I apologise. So HVO, they wanted to -- he wanted them to jointly deblock Sarajevo. Do you know why he then had a conflict with the Supreme Command and the head of the Bosnian state himself, because they did not want that? They needed Sarajevo to be blockaded, and if anyone was to deblock it, then it was not the Croat but the HVO army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, there were all sorts of stories, and this was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: After that, attacks on Juka began, the conflict with Zuka arose, so on and so forth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That happened on Igman. I do not know exactly. We assumed a different reason. Perhaps that was the reason; I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you tell me why is it that a Supreme Command did not want the deblocking of Sarajevo, the BiH armies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: How can I know that? We can only make our guesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, give me one of those, one of your guesses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know. Whatever I say will be silly. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: After that, when you arrived in Mostar and so on and so forth, all that you told my learned friend, you then begin to work as a driver. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Later on, not at first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. That's what I mean, later on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, at that time, Siroki Brijeg was the only free territory where all the logistics converged because there was fighting in Mostar. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Where the chief logistics was, I don't know. Yes, there was fighting in Mostar, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And there was no fighting in Siroki Brijeg. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And it is also the nearest town to Croatia, to ports, to ships and so on and so forth. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the humanitarian convoys arriving from all other parts of the world, did they go through Siroki?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the drivers from other units, from other brigades and whatever other units, did also go to the depots and work houses in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me -- I'm sorry, you do not have these permits in front of you, so I will ask the usher to give them to you because I would like to talk a little bit about them. Exhibit Number 501, 507. And please, Exhibit Number 242. Could you be kind enough to look at the permit signed by Miljenko Lasic and Petar Zelenika. It's Exhibit Number P242. It's written on the bottom of the page. Could you please turn to the Croatian text. Do you know who issued that permit to you personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Personally, by Juka Prazina or Bozo Sajin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you do not know personally who went to get the permit, who signed it, who the people were involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: You could only acknowledge it through the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, the date is February 6th. When did you come to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: January, was it, February?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It was the beginning. It was either January, February, March. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm asking this for a simple reason. And I will use this as a proposal of evidence by the Defence counsel, because the order that came from the Ministry of Defence was on February 16th, 1993, when you were established as an independent unit. You do not know. All right. Do you know who Zelenika was? It was stated that he was your commander, and that is why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, he could have been the commander of my commander. My commander was Juka. And I heard that he was the commander of the HVO, a minister, but I personally do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is all right. It is clearly stated on the permit. The overall commander signs it, and then your direct commander. Because according to this permit, that your direct commander was Mr. Zelenika, and Juka's commander was Mr. Zelenika. And Miljenko Lasic was commander of the operative zone of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is also clearly stated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: After that, could you please turn to Exhibit 507. Here your direct commander was Ivan Andabak and your commander of the Operative Zone was Mica Lasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That's how it is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You have it in front of you. Is that what is written there? So you personally just received this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, please go to Exhibit 501. You can see the date, "July 7th"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you received an open-ended permit, and then later on you take another permit, although you have this permit that has no limitation. I think you have been informed of that permit for July 7th and the next permit which was for free movement in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This permit was for going to Croatia? Well, I may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Here we see the signature "Valentin Coric."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us who has superior authority here, if someone gives you permission to move around Bosnia and Herzegovina freely and someone else makes it possible for you to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really say who is commander of whom. Here it is stated that the main commander seems to be nothing, so it's not quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, when you asked for permission, you referred to Juka, and then someone would bring it, either him or someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you kindly look at 303. Could you please -- I think on the left-hand side, you have the signature of Mladen Naletilic, Tuta; on the right-hand side, Prazina. Would Prazina himself sign? Could he perhaps sign instead of someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, it is something that we all know, but we could all sign on behalf of someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Prazina's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No. I have seen many of his signatures like that. I can recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you compare Prazina and Naletilic? Do you see any similarity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see Mr. Bos is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have an objection to this question. Our witness is not an expert in writing, so I don't think he can be asked this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please raise your question again, because Defence counsel lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: My objection is that this witness is not a writing expert, so I don't think he is allowed to be asked this question or to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, maybe you could tell us, where are you going to lead us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree and I confirm that this witness is not a handwriting expert. Well, the Defence will bring expertise when this is necessary. But we, who speak this language and write in the Latin script, you can see a great deal of similarity, not only, well, on the basis of the pencil used -- pen used, but this can even be seen just at first glance. This was my sole intention in asking the question. I have no further questions regarding the permit, because the Defence will investigate the issue further when it has its own witnesses. And now finally, as concerns the permissions, it's Exhibit 657.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We don't have the Document 657. We only have 659.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 659, 659. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again we have a new situation. Do you have the text in front of you, the Croatian version? Here your immediate commander is Bozo Sajin, and his commander is Marinko Mikulic. Do you know who Marinko Mikulic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No. I heard about him, but I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did he give you the same permission to travel to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, about you and your unit. Well, it seems that you received salaries from Juka, that this was not too good at the beginning but that the situation had improved later on. Who actually gave salaries? You always received money from Juka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, someone else sometimes distributed the salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said, in your statement to our learned colleagues, that you had seen Tuta once, only once, in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I had seen him several times, but I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The question refers to the Heliodrom. In the statement that you made to the investigators --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: -- you said that it was on January 1st, 1994, when all the units had been dissolved and a new unit was formed, the 2nd Guard Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, the 2nd was being formed, but the exact date --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, this is what you said in your statement. So that was the time you saw him at Heliodrom, when there was the ceremony for the founding of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just asking what you do know. Just a moment, Your Honours. Your Honour, the Defence has Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. concluded its cross-examination. We don't see that we have any question that we can put to the witness and expect a relevant answer, so I have concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. The witness, in his testimony, did not give a reason for the Defence of Vinko Martinovic to proceed to cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Clark has a question to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness S [sic], I'm not quite clear about your position in your unit after your -- sorry. Witness S [sic], I'm not quite clear about a couple of things. You gave evidence that when your leader, Juka Prazina, left, you were then without a commander, and you said that you were informed that Tuta was your commander. Who was immediately in command before you went up there? Who would have been your brigade commander? Witness T, it should be.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: After Juka had left, Bozo Sajin took over. He replaced him, and he told us who our chief commander was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did this gentleman, Bozo Sajin, did he remain your immediate officer for a period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, until the 2nd Guard Brigade was formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That brings me to the next question. When the 2nd Guard Brigade was formed and you joined it, who was your immediate officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: My immediate officer in the Guard Brigade was -- Rafo was the main person in the unit, in the battalion. Rafo was the main person of the battalion. The name of the other person, I do not know. [Realtime transcript read in error "Ralf"]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could you spell Rafo, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting you, Judge Clark. In the transcript, it says "Ralf" and not "Rafo," as the witness said. I think that's quite a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. That's why I was asking him to spell it, because it looks like a German name there. How do you spell "Rafo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: R-a-f-o.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. And you said that it was the 2nd Guard Brigade. And in that brigade, if I understand you correctly, you said there were many different ethnic groups, including several Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, there was a minority group of Muslims in the Guard Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And did you have -- did you serve as soldiers actively with weapons, or did you merely guard the munitions or supplies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 2nd Guard Brigade or something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The 2nd Guard Brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: As soldiers, with weapons. As soldiers with weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Does that mean that all your -- all the members of your 2nd Guard Brigade were in active service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, Witness T. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness T, I would have two questions for you. Your permits, you received a certain number of permits. They all bear different signatures. Did it ever happen that permits be signed by one single authority, but was it ever the case that there was always a double signature: one representative of a single authority and another signature from somebody else? Can you explain to us why on some permits, there are two signatures appearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, on one permit, you have the signature of the main commander of that area, and then the commander, the signature of the commander of that group, of that unit in which the person requesting the permit is from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there are permits where only one signature appears. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I'm not -- I don't understand. It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is my question not clear for you, or is the situation not clear for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I'm not clear about the signatures. If on one side, we have the signature of a commander of a sector, and after ten days, I get another permit, there will be another commander. And then other commanders will sign subsequent permits. That's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. The people who signed these permits, among them is Mladen Naletilic. Did you ever speak in person to that person? Did you ever see that person on the ground? Did you ever see him giving orders to local commanders on the ground? Could you ever observe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness T.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions out of Judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one question in relation to the question raised by Judge Clark regarding the person named Bozo Sajin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness T, you testified that Bozo Sajin took over command of the KB Krusko when Juka had left. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What was Bozo Sajin's function when Juka was still there in the unit? Was he also a member of the unit then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, he was member of that unit then, and he was Juka's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So when Juka left, the deputy became the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise about all these -- asking about the signatures on the permits. When Judge Diarra spoke about the fact that there were no permits -- not always two permits [sic] on Exhibit 507, there are also two signatures by two different persons, because there are always signatures by the two commanders. I will explain why this was so and how the HVO was organised, and there was a procedure with these signatures. But I will not go into that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think you will explain to us as a witness on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I simply want to say to Judge Diarra, there is not a single permit without both signatures. They both carry two -- all of them carry two signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
